sections.html:
Everything recorded in Mohave County, from deeds and mortgages to liens, releases, affidavits and plats, goes through the Recorder. The main office is at 700 West Beale Street in Kingman, phone (928) 753-0701. Mail goes to P.O. Box 7000, Kingman, AZ 86402. All offices close on observed holidays.

The county stretches across 13,461 square miles of northwest Arizona, so the Recorder keeps three counters. A seller in Bullhead City or Lake Havasu City doesn't need to drive to the county seat.

  • Kingman (main office): 700 West Beale Street, (928) 753-0701, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Bullhead City: 1130 Hancock Rd, (928) 758-0701 ext. 2026, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Thursday, closed noon to 1 p.m.
  • Lake Havasu City: 2001 College Dr, Ste 93, (928) 453-0702 ext. 3021, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., closed noon to 1 p.m.

Staff won't word a deed for you or decide whose name belongs on it. They treat those as legal questions and send you to an attorney, a title company or a paralegal.

A standard deed costs $30.00 to record. The same flat charge applies to all documents unless the schedule below says otherwise, as it has since July 1, 2019 (A.R.S. 11-475). Price doesn't affect it, although the Affidavit of Property Value filed with the deed asks what you were paid. Make checks out to the Mohave County Recorder.

ServiceMohave County fee
Recording, all documents unless otherwise specified$30.00
Instruments from governmental agencies$15.00
Copies of records, per page$1.00
Certification, per document$3.00
Conformed copy, each$1.50
Military dischargesNo charge (A.R.S. 11-465)
Subdivision plat, first page / each added page$24.00 / $20.00

Credit cards work at the counter and on the self-service site, with a transaction charge added.

sections.h2: Transfer tax and the Affidavit of Property Value
sections.html:
Nothing on the Recorder's schedule rises with the sale price. Arizona's constitution (Article 9, Section 24) forbids the state, counties and cities from adding a tax, fee or stamp requirement on selling real property, and only charges in place on December 31, 2007 remain.

What you do get is paperwork. Under A.R.S. 11-1133, a deed that transfers title carries an Affidavit of Property Value, signed by both sides or their agents. The form wants the parties' names and addresses, the legal description, street address, parcel number, sale date, total consideration and the type of financing. Leave it incomplete and the recorder must refuse the deed, unless a valid exemption is noted.

The page-two exemption list on the form is where you find the exemption number to print on the document, if one applies.

The exempt transfers are listed in A.R.S. 11-1134, and whichever exemption you rely on must be written on the face of the deed. A few come up often when a family is settling an estate or a divorce.

  • Gifts, and quitclaim deeds where no money changes hands.
  • Property that moves because a court ordered it.
  • Homes passed for token consideration among spouses, parents and children, grandparents and grandchildren, or siblings.
  • Trustee's deeds after a deed of trust power of sale, and transfers that give or release security for a debt.
  • Moves into or out of a trust for token consideration, whether person to trustee or trustee to beneficiary.
  • Corrective deeds that confirm or fix one already on record.

A regular sale, cash buyer or not, fits none of these and needs the full affidavit. Doubtful about an exemption? Put the question to the closing title company first.

A signed, notarized original can be brought to any of the three counters. Mailing is the other option, with the fee enclosed, to the Kingman post office box (P.O. Box 7000, ZIP 86402). Staff test the document against A.R.S. 11-480, assign a recording number and make it permanent record. Walk-ins leave with the original after it is scanned. Mail takes roughly 4 to 6 weeks to come back. Indexers then enter the parties and parcel, which is what makes the deed searchable.

Once something is recorded, it stays on record, period. A faulty legal description or a misspelled name needs a second, corrective document and a second fee. Read the deed twice before handing it over.

A free Recorded Document Search sits on the Recorder's self-service site; type last name first in the both-name fields. Copies are $1.00 a page, ordered in person, online, by mail or on the phone at (928) 753-0701. To find the right record, give the book and page, the fee number, the recording date or the names on it. Include a stamped return envelope with a mailed request.

A clean search result isn't a guarantee the property is free of liens. Title insurance is what protects you. If back taxes, a judgment or a lien might be attached to your house, order a title search before you list so you know what has to be cleared at closing. Staff will show you how to search but won't do the research.

Mohave had 213,267 residents in 2020 and 117,650 housing units, of which 22.4% sat vacant. Owners occupied 71.7% of the occupied homes. For a rural parcel outside the cities, zoning, permits and septic questions belong to Development Services at (928) 757-0903.

The Recorder passes recorded documents to the Assessor, who changes the owner on the tax roll. More than 200 recorded documents reach the Assessor every day, so ownership updates move through a queue. Recording a legal document is the only way to change the owner name on real property.

If you still receive a tax bill after closing, forward it to the new owner or mail it to P.O. Box 712, Kingman, AZ 86402 with a note that the property was sold. Tax amounts, due dates and appeals are in the Mohave County property tax guide.

One order of events works well. Sign the deed and affidavit at the title company, let the title company record them, then ask for the recorded copy and keep it. A cash buyer's closing follows the same order, but with no lender there is no new deed of trust to record behind yours.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Mohave County, AZ?
faqs.a: The charge is $30.00 per document under A.R.S. 11-475, in effect since July 1, 2019. Government agency instruments are $15.00, copies run $1.00 a page and certification is $3.00 a document.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax in Mohave County?
faqs.a: No fee on the schedule rises with the price. Arizona's constitution, Article 9, Section 24, bars new taxes or fees on conveying real property, apart from charges that existed on December 31, 2007. A completed Affidavit of Property Value still goes with the deed.

faqs.q: Where can I record a deed in Mohave County?
faqs.a: The main office is at 700 West Beale Street, Kingman, AZ 86401, (928) 753-0701. Branch counters are at 1130 Hancock Rd in Bullhead City and 2001 College Dr, Ste 93 in Lake Havasu City, both closed noon to 1 p.m.

faqs.q: May I mail my deed to the Mohave County Recorder?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the original to P.O. Box 7000, Kingman, AZ 86402 with the correct fee. It is scanned and sent back to your return address, usually in 4 to 6 weeks.

faqs.q: Will the Mohave County Recorder tell me whose name goes on my deed?
faqs.a: No, because that is legal advice. Staff refer you to an attorney, title company or paralegal. They can explain how to search records and submit a document.
